name: Colchic Rainforests and Wetlands
description: Along an 80-kilometre stretch of Georgia's Black Sea coast, seven protected areas preserve damp, ancient forests and peat bogs that rise from sea level to peaks above 2,500 metres. Many plants and animals here are relics from before the Ice Ages. The wetlands shelter the critically endangered Colchic sturgeon and serve as a vital rest stop for migrating birds funnelling past Batumi.
